nodes.title: Bind physical step equations to the represented integration interval
implementation: Use one planning value containing represented t_start, t_end and consumed h_eff; require t_end > t_start and verify the addition/subtraction relationship explicitly.

In the local Sterbenz regime choose t_end from the nominal proposal and targets, then h_eff=t_end-t_start; pass that same h_eff through stage equations, dense extension, error/controller history and work receipt.

Recheck user max_step and method constraints against h_eff, not the nominal h; if the next representable endpoint would exceed a hard maximum, report time-resolution failure instead of silently enlarging the step.
Outside exact subtraction regime retain a documented multi-piece or compensated local-clock policy; do not claim the local prototype solves opposite-sign cancellation globally.
Check internal Radau/BDF half-step clocks separately; outer-step advancement does not prove each substep advances.
Feed actual successive h_eff to variable-step BDF coefficients, or explicitly restart BDF history where the fixed-step coefficient assumptions fail.
acceptance: Constant flow on the 8-ULP span at t0=+-1e12 with nominal h=1e-4 reaches y(tf)=1 within 1e-12 or returns a typed failure; no successful 0.8192 endpoint.
Repeat identical local problem with time origin 0, large positive/negative origins and power-of-two unit changes; distinguish representational conditioning from truncation.
Check exact requested endpoints, adjacent interior samples, hard stops, opposite-sign crossing and below-ULP steps.
Check nonautonomous analytic problems and BDF history/order with changed effective h, including power-of-two ULP boundaries.
Every successful recorded step has a receipt connecting physical h, represented endpoints and all accepted internal reports.
nodes.failure_status: Typed time-resolution or inconsistent-clock failure; never silently relabel a state to an unintegrated physical time.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Standalone candidate checks constant-flow local clock consistency only; production, nonautonomous order and full BDF history still require implementation and tests.

nodes.title: Make nonzero-span output endpoint ownership unambiguous
implementation: For nonzero spans require at least two represented output points and require actual endpoints in the output schedule.
Reject uniform grids whose rounded interval count is zero for a nonzero span; do not let an epoch-scaled validation tolerance certify divisibility.
Adopt strict endpoint equality, as in the standalone candidate, or expose an explicit endpoint-alias policy returning canonical actual timestamps and separate requested labels.
Keep one-point schedules valid only for an exactly zero span.
acceptance: uniform(1e12,nextafter^4(1e12),1) rejects as indivisible or produces both true endpoints with a documented rule; it must not silently emit only y0 labelled tf.
Explicit [tf] for t0<tf is rejected.
Two adjacent distinct endpoint values remain distinct, including subnormal and large-epoch spans.
The valid [t0,tf] control integrates to the analytic final value, while shifted endpoint labels are either rejected or canonically reported with alias metadata.
Dense and clipped collectors produce identical endpoint semantics.
nodes.failure_status: Typed invalid-schedule error before integration; no success receipt with initial state at the final timestamp.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Minimal admission contract only; production API compatibility decision remains with maintainers.

nodes.title: Separate fixed-grid construction from long-run accumulated clock drift
implementation: Define fixed-step grid ownership by indexed or compensated local timestamps, including exact final landing.
Base BDF history on actual intervals; do not merely enlarge a tolerance to hide an extra step.
Version the research replay clock policy explicitly before changing sealed research-driver histories.
acceptance: 1000 nominal steps of 0.01 on (0,10) have the documented grid count without a final roundoff micro-step.
BDF startup count and applied-order history match the chosen grid policy; endpoint accuracy remains controlled.
Existing sealed research replays retain identity or receive a distinct, documented policy version and new evidence.
nodes.failure_status: Preserve the documented existing limitation until the new grid contract is tested; no generic fixed-step invariance claim.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Only the stated acceptance contract; no automatic production or performance promotion

nodes.title: Bind weighting loss to original-target convergence
implementation: Introduce weighting quality/transform-error status in action reports, including prefix and dense wrappers.
Minimal safe behavior rejects lost>0 before successful original-target convergence unless a trusted output bound is supplied.
Keep the work counter; do not mistake it for an acceptance bound.
acceptance: R3 positive and negative h nilpotent witnesses cannot report unqualified original-target convergence.
Original PHI-R1/R2 fixtures remain within 1e-12.
A=0 control documents conservative rejection or bounded acceptance.
No report consumer can discard non-authoritative transform status.
deliverables: native regression stdout/exit and source hash
nodes.claim_ceiling: Closes unsafe partial-loss success; does not implement general full-range action arithmetic.

nodes.title: Propagate coefficient rounding to physical output
implementation: Represent coefficient rounding/loss bounds using mantissa/exponent or interval arithmetic; never round a nonzero bound down to zero.
Offer structural action bounds for nilpotent/triangular/dissipative cases and fail closed for unsupported general operators.
Separate transform, projection, truncation, and roundoff error fields.
acceptance: Exact nilpotent Fraction fixtures with positive/negative h bound the actual first-component error.
Normal, subnormal and near-overflow inputs exercise each bound branch.
Cases with only a coarse logarithmic-norm bound remain rejected when too conservative; do not relax tolerance.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Only certified operator classes and implemented rounding model; no generic matrix-free certificate.

nodes.title: Preserve dense reference amplitude/transform authority at consumers
implementation: Use a report-returning fused dense interface carrying amplitude flags and weighting loss.
Consumer classifies flagged reference as NotEvaluated unless an independent higher-precision/structural oracle resolves it.
Retain raw flags in comparison records rather than only a vector.
acceptance: diag(700,-700) mixed-range witness is not admitted as a precision oracle silently.
Homogeneous scalar amplitude sweep retains accuracy and authority.
Demonstrate actual final gate behavior with injected flagged report.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Reference authority correctness, not a claim that existing G3 campaigns are invalid.

nodes.title: Separate range-safe budget evaluation from certified budget lower bound
implementation: Keep current range-safe nearest-rounded budget as a diagnostic API.
Implement explicit outward rounding or analytic error enclosure for mantissa ratio, integer power, product and subnormal conversion.
Return an uncertainty interval and explicit certificate status.
acceptance: Exact represented-input rational encloses current R2-POL-01 fixture.
Boundary cases one ULP around each branch do not falsely accept.
Zero, underflow, overflow, minimum step and maximum supported exponent have explicit semantics.
nodes.claim_ceiling: A verified arithmetic budget bound does not certify the numerical output-error estimate.
